facts.statement: Branta rhuax, known as the giant Hawaii goose, was an extinct species of goose found only on the island of Hawaii.
facts.quote: Branta rhuax, the giant Hawaii goose, is an extinct goose endemic to the island of Hawaii.

facts.statement: The fossil bones were found near Kaumaikeohu, above Pahala in the Kau District of the Island of Hawaii, beneath a prehistoric lava flow and on top of an ash bed.
facts.quote: The bones were found at a depth of beneath a prehistoric lava flow, on top of an ash bed, near Kaumaikeohu, above Pahala in the Kau District of the Island of Hawaii.

facts.statement: The fossil bones were friable and warped because they were subjected to intense heat from the lava.
facts.quote: The bones are friable and warped, having been subjected to intense heat from the lava.

facts.statement: The specific epithet 'rhuax' is derived from the Greek word for lava stream.
facts.quote: The specific epithet comes from the Greek rhuax (lava stream).

facts.statement: The holotype is a fragmentary right tibiotarsus held by the United States National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C.
facts.quote: The holotype is a fragmentary right tibiotarsus (USNM V16740) held by the United States National Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C.

facts.statement: It was the first fossil bird ever described from the Hawaiian Islands.
facts.quote: It was the first fossil bird to be described from the Hawaiian Islands.

facts.statement: Olson and James (1991) considered the available material too imperfect to determine the bird's affinities precisely, suggesting its relationships remained doubtful until more specimens were found.
facts.quote: However, subsequently Olson and James (1991) considered that the available material was too imperfect for determining the affinities so precisely and that the relationships of the bird would remain doubtful until further specimens were obtained.

facts.statement: The genus Geochen belongs to the family Anatidae.
The species lived during the Holocene epoch, from 0.0117 million years ago to the present.
facts.quote: Time range: Holocene to Holocene (0.0117 to 0 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The bird was described in 1943 by Alexander Wetmore from subfossil remains originally discovered in 1926, in the course of a public works excavation of a water supply tunnel.

rejected.statement: The species was initially described as the monotypic genus Geochen but was reassigned to the genus Branta by Storrs L. Olson in 2013 based on reexamination of material and DNA data.
rejected.quote: It was initially described as the monotypic genus Geochen, but then reassigned to Branta by Storrs L. Olson in 2013 after reexamination of the subfossil material and based on earlier DNA sequence data.
